google.note: Create a project, enable the APIs you want (Calendar, Gmail), then create an OAuth client ID of type "Desktop app": that type allows a loopback redirect on any port, which is what local-kody uses, and it needs no redirect URI typed in. On the consent screen, add yourself as a test user. Default scope is calendar read-only; add --scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly for mail. Without access_type=offline there is no refresh token, so the preset sets it.

linear.note: Linear matches the redirect URI exactly, so register http://127.0.0.1:8765/callback and keep the fixed port.

notion.note: Notion authenticates the token request with HTTP Basic and matches the redirect URI exactly: register http://127.0.0.1:8765/callback. Its tokens do not expire, so there is nothing to refresh.

github.note: An OAuth app (not a GitHub App) matches the callback URL exactly: register http://127.0.0.1:8765/callback. Tokens do not expire unless the app opts in.
